quality: Candidate visual pass: coherent pale-stone coastal chest, fully framed in all four original captures, with consistent desktop/mobile appearance. The exact marketing retains the same broad silhouette and decorative forms; richer contact shadows and metal shading are a promotional finish gap, not demonstrated breakage.
hardware: Long brass front clasp, corner fittings and pale block feet correspond to marketing. Open originals show two rear hinges and the released clasp projecting above the lid. No visibly missing fitting or definite detached part; stills do not certify attachment or motion.
terrain: Turquoise inset, pink curved shore and thick pale arch are preserved. The arch reads as a sculptural handle and the shore as a smooth ribbon in both reference and captures. The exterior lid decoration is naturally hidden from this front-facing open view, not proven absent.
texture: Soft cloudy limestone-like mottling is visible, with a somewhat regular appearance across large open surfaces. Browser brass and stone lack the reference's shading richness; no texture-loading failure established.
limitations: Read source_readme.md: abstract arch, opaque glossy water, no surveyed geography or photographic equivalence. Small mobile support text and limited fine-detail readability remain. Review covers endpoint images only, not continuous motion, collision certification, physical-phone performance or user approval.
decision: Accept as a stylized candidate with disclosed real-time finish limitations; do not label as photoreal or exact promotional rendering parity.

decision: Accept stylized candidate with blue-hole depth and material-polish caveats. Do not describe the obvious teal seam as a failed closure solely from these stills.

decision: Owner decision required: accept the intentionally stylized plaster/timber and faceted-mountain direction with appropriately aligned marketing, or request a separate fidelity revision. Do not claim exact promotional parity or classify this as proven broken geometry.

decision: Accept stylized candidate with explicit fiber-detail and promotional-finish caveats; no proven hardware omission found after original-image inspection.

quality: Strong recognizable red floral chest, completely framed in all originals, with no obvious catastrophic geometry or layout issue. Exact marketing nevertheless promises more defined floral composition and richer irregular surface finish than the softer real-time candidate.
hardware: Long central clasp, separate round front disc, left ring pull, corner caps and block feet are visible and broadly correspond to marketing. Open originals expose two hinges and a projecting released clasp; no definite detached hardware established. Satin-metal response is flatter in captures.
terrain: No geographic terrain intended. Three raised rounded floral clusters and paired front diamond groups survive. Marketing distinguishes grooved centers, angular connecting stems and scattered leaf accents more clearly; captures read as simplified petal clusters with less legible stem/leaf composition. This establishes appearance mismatch, not missing mesh proof.
texture: Marketing is deep red with fine irregular wood-like/lacquer variation. Browser is brighter vermilion with smooth highlights and broad regular horizontal tonal bands, especially on open lid underside. Repetition/banding and simplified relief are finish/fidelity concerns, not proven corrupt textures.
limitations: Source readme discloses thick rounded stylized florals, simpler angular leaves/stems, intentional dark seam, nonhistorical family hardware and invented interior. It also records a corrected historical petal-seating failure; current stills do not establish that failure persists. No photoreal parity, user approval or motion certification inferred.
decision: Owner decision required on accepting the simplified floral/lacquer direction versus tightening reference fidelity or aligning marketing. Keep the visible ornament/material gap distinct from unproven mechanical or loading defects.
